description: We are a brother and sister duo, intrigued by the interconnection of astronomy and technology. Our skills include coding (python, r, html, css), and a deep interest in satellites and rovers.
summary:
Moon maps is a web tool that compares lunar south pole landing sites and dates by where the Sun and Earth sit above the local horizon. Users choose two scenarios, each a site and start date (or any coordinates), and see Sun and Earth elevation charts plus metrics: percent sunlit, percent Earth in view, time with both, and the longest dark spell and communication gap.

It addresses the challenge by turning power potential and direct-to-Earth communication windows into a quick side-by-side comparison for planners, educators and the public. Using NASA data, we built terrain-aware results from LRO LOLA elevation maps and JPL Horizons Sun and Earth directions. In a 30-day example, Malapert Massif had Earth in view 100% of the time, while Nobile Rim 2 had Sun and Earth together only 6.2% of the time.

This matters because sunlight and Earth contact, not just safe terrain, decide whether a south pole mission can operate. The web page uses an in-browser lunar ephemeris checked against reference values, with an adjustable horizon mask. Embedding the full NASA terrain data is our next step.
